lesson:
Use element visibility assertions instead of networkidle waits when background polling prevents the network from becoming idle.
When writing Playwright tests for pages that contain components performing periodic server requests which keep the network active indefinitely.
The `page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')` wait fails or times out if any component on the page polls its server periodically. In this case, a support chat widget polled every 20 seconds, preventing the network from ever being idle for the required duration.

Replace the global network state check with a specific assertion that waits for the relevant UI element to be visible:

```javascript
await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Order history' })).toBeVisible()
```

This approach finishes quickly once the content is rendered, regardless of background network activity.
detail: deferred/distill-review: The lesson generalizes a specific limit (the chat widget comes from the shared page layout) into a broader rule about any component performing periodic requests.

lesson:
Scope break-inside rules to specific selectors instead of applying them globally, because broad application can clip content like footnotes while leaving other elements intact.
When using Paged.js or similar print CSS tools and observing that long footnotes or call-outs are clipped by the bottom margin due to overflow handling.
The clipping occurred because `break-inside: avoid` was applied to both `.footnote-area` and call-out boxes. Removing it from `.footnote-area` resolved the clipping on page 14 without affecting the call-outs.

This fix was verified only for the single-column rulebook layout; the two-column supplement was not rebuilt, so its behavior remains unknown.
detail: deferred/distill-review: The lesson generalizes the specific fix into a broad rule about scoping break-inside rules globally, which stretches the source's context where the issue was caused by the rule applying to call-out boxes as well.

  leaving other elements intact.

The clipping occurred because `break-inside: avoid` was applied to both `.footnote-area` and call-out boxes. Removing it from `.footnote-area` resolved the clipping on page 14 without affecting the call-outs.

This fix was verified only for the single-column rulebook layout; the two-column supplement was not rebuilt, so its behavior remains unknown.
